sources.title: The Barankin bound and threshold behavior in frequency estimation
sources.venue: IEEE Transactions on Signal Processing 45(9), 2398–2401; DOI 10.1109/78.622965
sources.publication_status: Published journal article confirmed by Ghent University author record; peer-review status not explicitly established on inspected evidence
sources.access_level: Abstract-only (IEEE abstract surfaced in search; IEEE open failed with HTTP 418; university record is metadata-only)
sources.content_locator: IEEE abstract returned by search: threshold effect occurs when Barankin bound departs materially from CR bound; SNR*T/ln(T) proposed as a threshold indicator for sinusoid in AWGN. Ghent University record lines 8–12, 76–90 confirms publication metadata.

findings.claim: A small nominal variance or CR-bound-like uncertainty is not enough to establish the proposed 95% / 0.10 Hz capture success rate: frequency estimators can enter a threshold/outlier region where actual error departs sharply from local CRB behavior.
findings.support_locator: Knockaert IEEE abstract: threshold when Barankin and Cramer–Rao bounds diverge; heuristic SNR*T/ln(T) indicator under sinusoid-in-AWGN assumptions. Kay abstract: its efficient estimator reaches ML-like performance only at moderately high SNR.
findings.decision_implication: Include empirical error quantiles, outlier rate, and false-publication controls alongside reported uncertainty; do not treat a finite covariance/interval as calibrated coverage. A nominal high integrated SNR does not establish threshold-free performance for the actual waveform.
findings.assumptions: The papers analyze sinusoidal frequency estimation with AWGN; SNR and T follow each paper's model and normalization.
findings.applicability_gap: The task's dB-Hz C/N0 values, reference level, envelope, auxiliary activity, search range and 137/4096 delivery are not directly interchangeable with paper SNR/sample-count settings. The threshold indicator is a diagnostic lead, not a feasibility verdict or project guarantee.
findings.next_discriminator: For each hypothesized offset and level, measure the full capture-level error distribution and outlier rate over independent noise/capture seeds at the actual acquisition deadline, with absent-tone controls; compare these with the estimator's claimed uncertainty.

findings.claim: Three-bin Fourier interpolation is a credible cheap precision comparator to a broad nonlinear fit: Quinn reports an estimator using only three Fourier components with asymptotic variance near the periodogram maximum-likelihood/CR lower bound, up to roughly three times that variance.
findings.support_locator: Macquarie author-university abstract lines 17–19; peer-reviewed/published record lines 14, 23–29.
findings.decision_implication: A low-cost FFT-seeded/interpolated estimate can be compared against the current measurement path before investing in heavier fitting; its reported asymptotics do not establish finite-sample success, robustness to multiple tones, ramps or intermittent support.
findings.assumptions: Sinusoidal component, periodogram/Fourier coefficients, asymptotic sample size.
findings.applicability_gap: Abstract-only evidence; it does not establish performance under the receiver's pilot amplitude shape, auxiliary activity, short apertures or frequency drift.
findings.next_discriminator: Use identical generated PCM and front-end selection to compare Quinn-style three-bin interpolation, existing short-aperture estimate, and a bounded local ML fit at 200 ms and longer coherent apertures; report compute, error tails and failures.

findings.claim: Efficient single-tone estimators can approach optimal ML performance under stated noise and signal assumptions, but estimator rankings are conditional: Kay's result is for one complex sinusoid in complex white Gaussian noise and says its simpler estimator matches ML at moderately high SNR; it also shows linear prediction can miss the CR bound even at high SNR.
findings.decision_implication: Keep a simple estimator as a practical contender, but select it from matched receiver captures rather than complexity labels or high-SNR asymptotics; avoid presuming linear-prediction or phase-difference methods are efficient without testing their exact observation model.
findings.assumptions: Single complex sinusoid, white Gaussian noise, moderately high SNR; no modulation/envelope or multiple-source complications described in inspected abstract.
findings.applicability_gap: Project's generated/helper tone may be real-valued and amplitude shaped; project excerpt H05 says phase-coherent cross-dwell fitting requires a coherence certificate, while native unknown per-hop phase lacks one. Those are supplied code facts, not runtime evidence.
findings.next_discriminator: On the same frequency-only capture slices, compare simple estimator and local ML/periodogram using real receiver data representation, both continuous and phase-reset boundaries; stratify by level, offset, chunk size, auxiliary activity and tone presence.

rejected_or_redundant: Did not pursue the Rife–Boorstyn classic beyond citation metadata: search supplied no accessible paper passage needed to answer the practical decision; no claim from that paper is used.

Did not pursue broad spectral/DOA or multi-tone subspace methods because the stated decision is frequency-only evidence for a generated helper tone and these would add model assumptions without resolving the immediate threshold/calibration question.
Did not use the ResearchGate author-uploaded Knockaert full-text lead as evidence; its publisher abstract and Ghent University publication record sufficed.
unresolved: No accessible full texts were inspected. Exact finite-record bounds under the project's real-signal/noisy-ramp/multiple-activity model remain unknown.

The source excerpts identify candidate coherence and amplitude-envelope conditions but no measured tracker performance. No supplied or researched paper establishes whether <=0.10 Hz by 6 s at >=95% is achievable for the hypothesized captures.
The dB-Hz reference-level conversion into each estimator's observation-SNR convention depends on signal/noise bandwidth and capture model, which were not established by the packet.
stop_reason: Three complementary primary journal findings answered the approach/validation question; remaining candidate searches were unlikely to change the discriminators. Stopped at 10/16 logical web operations and well within the 12-minute target.
escalation_ready: Yes. Sol/Astra can decide whether to run the small matched-capture comparison: an FFT three-bin interpolation comparator, one simple high-SNR estimator, and the existing/local ML path; validate capture-level tails, claimed uncertainty calibration and absent-tone admission under true chunk/coherence/envelope conditions. Research supports these as candidates and cautions, not a preferred architecture or feasibility conclusion.
